overview: Single-clinic implementation study during 2027, guided by RE-AIM, in which three adaptations are introduced in sequence: an orientation call and a hybrid video option from the first 2027 group, and an evening group once staff hours are approved. People who leave early are followed up briefly, and conversations with leavers and completers are organised by CFIR constructs.
population: All adults referred to and starting the group programme in 2027, and the programme staff; baseline cohorts are the 184 starters of the previous 18 months.
exposure: Orientation call (20 minutes, by the nurse practitioner, before session 1); hybrid option (join any session by video); evening group (if approved).
procedures: At referral the clinic records employment, main travel mode, language spoken at home and interpreter need. Attendance is recorded at every session. People who miss two consecutive sessions receive a call offering a brief outcome check and a 20-minute conversation. All starters receive the pain interference questionnaire at the first session, the last session or the point of leaving, and at three months. Fidelity to the eight core session topics is checked by a session checklist.

outcomes.name: Completion of six or more sessions
outcomes.measure: Proportion of starters attending six or more of eight sessions, by group and adaptation
outcomes.why: The implementation outcome the clinic is failing on.

outcomes.name: Reach
outcomes.measure: Proportion of referred people who start, overall and by employment, travel mode and language
outcomes.why: Shows whether the adaptations bring in people who used to decline.

outcomes.name: Pain interference
outcomes.measure: Three-item pain, enjoyment and activity scale at start, end or leaving, and three months
outcomes.timing: Start, end or leaving, three months
outcomes.why: Checks the benefit is kept for completers and measured for leavers.

outcomes.name: Group connection
outcomes.measure: Two-item rating of connection with the group at the last attended session
outcomes.why: Video participation may weaken what makes the group work.

outcomes.name: Fidelity to core content
outcomes.measure: Proportion of the eight core topics delivered per group
outcomes.why: Separates a failed adaptation from a diluted programme.

feasibility: The orientation call and hybrid option use existing staff and the hospital video platform; the evening group needs the unapproved hours. Follow-up calls take about two hours a week of nurse practitioner time.
biasMitigation: Barriers recorded at referral before anyone leaves
Leavers contacted by someone who does not run their group
Fidelity checklist for adapted and standard groups
Adaptation start dates recorded and marked on the completion chart

biasFlags.label: Secular change in referrals
biasFlags.note: The waiting list and referral mix may change during 2027; compare characteristics of starters by period.

biasFlags.label: Low response from people who leave
biasFlags.note: The main threat to the effectiveness measure; report response by group.

biasFlags.label: Overlapping adaptations
biasFlags.note: Sequential introduction limits but does not remove overlap.

flags: One balancing and one process measure
Three recorded barrier variables used for stratified reporting
parsimony.simplestPath: One clinic, one primary implementation outcome, adaptations in sequence, brief follow-up of leavers.

theoreticalFramework: RE-AIM for outcomes and CFIR for conversations with leavers and staff; no other framework.
summary: Sequenced adaptations with completion as the primary implementation outcome and follow-up of people who leave.
